classification.difficultyReason: Combine literal speed, a multiplicative speed comparison and travel time to derive a distance formula.

content.prompt: A train that travels $a$ km at a constant speed in $b$ hours is $p$ times as fast as a bus. If the bus takes $m$ hours to cover the distance between two places, how many kilometres apart are the two places?

answer.short:
$\dfrac{am}{bp}$ km.

Divide the train’s speed by $p$, then multiply by the bus’s travel time.
answer.worked:
The train’s speed is $\dfrac{a}{b}$ km/h. Since the train is $p$ times as fast as the bus,
$$\begin{align*}\text{Bus speed}&=\frac{a}{b}\div p\\\text{Bus speed}&=\frac{a}{bp}\text{ km/h}.\end{align*}$$
Using distance $=$ speed $\times$ time,
$$\begin{align*}\text{Distance}&=\frac{a}{bp}\times m\\\text{Distance}&=\frac{am}{bp}\text{ km}.\end{align*}$$
